<explanation>
1. Project Type & Purpose  
   - GitNexus V2 is primarily a _client‐side, single‐page application_ (React + Vite + Tailwind) that embeds a full graph‐based code intelligence engine inside the browser using WebAssembly.  
   - It also ships a lightweight Node.js “MCP” (Microservice Companion Protocol) server (`gitnexus-mcp`) to expose its capabilities to external editor tools via WebSockets/CLI.  

2. High-Level Architecture Components  
   a. Frontend (Browser SPA)  
      • React UI (App.tsx + Components)  
      • Vite build + Tailwind CSS  
      • Sigma.js WebGL graph visualization (GraphCanvas)  
      • Web Workers + Comlink for off-thread processing  
   b. Core Engine (all WASM)  
      • Tree-sitter WASM module: AST parsing for up to 9 languages  
      • KuzuDB WASM: Graph database + HNSW vector index  
      • Embedding model (snowflake-arctic-embed-xs) in WebGPU/WASM  
   c. Ingestion & Indexing Pipeline (phases P1–P7)  
      • ZIP loader → file enumeration → folder/file nodes  
      • AST generation → symbol table build  
      • IMPORTS & CALLS edge creation with confidence scoring  
      • Leiden clustering → MEMBER_OF edges  
      • Entry‐point BFS → STEP_IN_PROCESS edges  
      • Background embedding → BM25 & vector index build  
   d. LLM Agent & Tools  
      • LangChain React agent orchestrating 7 Smart Tools (search, cypher, grep, read, overview, explore, impact)  
      • Precomputed graph structure fed into tools for decision‐ready context  
   e. MCP Server (gitnexus-mcp)  
      • CLI entrypoint + `serve` command  
      • WebSocket server + Bridge/Protocol layer (protocol.ts, websocket-server.ts)  
      • Exposes the same Smart Tools over MCP for external IDEs  

3. Relationships & Data Flows  
   - User uploads or drags ZIP → Frontend  
   - Main thread delegates file I/O & parsing to Web Worker  
   - Worker loads Tree-sitter WASM, produces ASTs → Symbol Table  
   - Frontend pipelines data into KuzuDB WASM, building nodes & edges  
   - After graph build, embeddings start in background → vector index  
   - UI queries graph & embedding indexes via Cypher/agent calls  
   - LLM agent issues tool calls; results render in UI panels  
   - Separately, `gitnexus-mcp` can point to local browser instance or load its own pipeline in Node  
   - External tool (e.g., Cursor) connects via WebSocket to MCP → issues Smart Tool calls → receives structured JSON  

4. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - _Zero‐Server SPA_: all compute lives in the browser via WebAssembly + Web Workers  
   - _Pipeline Pattern_: seven clearly delineated indexing phases with progress tracking  
   - _Graph + Vector Unified Storage_: KuzuDB with native HNSW index, no external DB  
   - _Agent Tooling_: LangChain ReAct agent wrapping precomputed graph context  
   - _Sidecar Microservice (MCP)_: Node.js companion exposing identical API for integrations  

5. Diagramming Guidelines  
   a. Draw a two‐column layout:  
      • Left: Browser components & flows  
      • Right: MCP server + external tool integrations  
   b. Use distinct shapes/colors:  
      • Frontend UI (rounded rectangles, e.g., React components in blue)  
      • WASM modules & Web Workers (cylinders or hexagons in green)  
      • Graph DB & Vector index (cylinder in orange)  
      • CLI/Server (squares in purple)  
      • External Consumers (dashed border boxes in grey)  
   c. Arrows & labels:  
      • Solid arrows for data flows (ZIP → Worker → DB → UI)  
      • Dashed arrows for control flows or API calls (UI → LLM Agent → Tools)  
      • Annotate edges with protocols (WebSocket, Comlink, Cypher, MCP)  
   d. Layer separation:  
      • UI Layer  
      • Compute Layer (Workers + WASM)  
      • Storage Layer (KuzuDB WASM)  
      • Integration Layer (MCP Server)  
   e. Call out indexing phases P1–P7 in a sub‐box under Compute Layer, with a simple linear flow chart.

6. Tailoring for This Project  
   - Emphasize _client‐side_ exclusively: no external servers.  
   - Show how Tree-sitter, KuzuDB, and Embeddings all load as WASM modules in the browser.  
   - Highlight the seven-phase indexing pipeline as a core architectural pillar.  
   - Illustrate the LangChain agent’s seven Smart Tools tapping precomputed graph structures.  
   - Depict the MCP sidecar’s protocol & WebSocket bridge as a separate integration point.  

7. Essential Diagram Elements  
   - Clear component labels (e.g., “Tree-sitter WASM”, “KuzuDB + HNSW”)  
   - Directional arrows annotated with data types or protocols  
   - Color coding/shapes for layers (UI vs. Compute vs. Storage vs. Integration)  
   - Sub‐diagrams for the Indexing Pipeline (P1–P7) and Agent Tools  
   - Legend or key to explain colors/shapes  

By breaking GitNexus into these well‐defined components and flows, your system design diagram will accurately reflect its zero‐server, graph‐centric architecture, guiding both maintainers and integrators through its internal workings.
